ruleName: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds: Stroke-and-Distance Relief
group: Play the Course as You Find It
imagePrompt: A modern, semi-realistic (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) illustration in a bright, engaging, junior golf quiz style. The scene shows a junior golfer at the teeing area of a golf hole, holding a club and watching their ball. The golf ball is in mid-air, clearly flying over and beyond a line of white stakes or a low fence marking the out of bounds area on one side of the hole. The setting makes it obvious that the ball is out of bounds. Tee markers are present, and the out of bounds area is clear. Show no text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A junior golfer stands by the teeing area, watching a golf ball fly over a line of white stakes marking the out of bounds; the ball is clearly out of bounds.

sceneSpec.setting: Teeing area of a golf hole with an out of bounds fence or white stakes marking the boundary on one side.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer, a junior, holding a club near the tee markers, watching their shot.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: One ball in mid-air flying well beyond the boundary fence or white stakes, clearly out of bounds.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment the player and others can see the ball has landed out of bounds beyond the markers.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Recognising the correct procedure when a ball is definitely out of bounds from the tee shot.
mustShow: Golf ball out of bounds beyond white stakes or a fence
Clearly marked out of bounds area
mustNotShow: Any text, labels, numbers, arrows or captions

questions.title: What To Do If Your Ball Goes Out of Bounds from the Tee
questions.question: You hit your ball from the tee and it goes out of bounds. What should you do next?

choices.text: Drop your ball next to where it went out of bounds.
Go to a special drop zone to hit your ball.
Hit another ball from the tee, where you first played, using stroke-and-distance.
Play your next shot from the fairway close to where it went out of bounds.

questions.explanation: If your ball goes out of bounds, you must play a new ball from the same spot as your last shot. Most times, that means going back to the tee and hitting again. You can’t drop the ball where it went out or use a drop zone unless there’s a special rule for that.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place off the golf course where you are not allowed to play, marked by white stakes or a line.
You play again from where you last hit and add one extra shot to your score.
A special place where you are sometimes allowed to drop your ball, used only if a special rule says so.

questions.teachingTip: Show where the out of bounds line is on the course. Practise hitting from the tee again to understand stroke-and-distance.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can just drop your ball near where it went out.
Believing you can use a drop zone without a special rule.
Wanting to hit from the edge of the fairway instead of returning to the tee.

questions.title: Tee Shot Out of Bounds
questions.question: Your tee shot is definitely out of bounds. What must you do?

choices.text: Drop beside where it crossed the boundary.
Play from a designated drop zone.
Play another ball from where the previous stroke was made under stroke and distance.
Play your next shot from the fairway near the boundary.

questions.explanation: When a ball is out of bounds, the player must take stroke-and-distance relief by playing another ball from as near as possible to the spot where the previous stroke was made (Rule 18.2). You do not drop beside where it crossed the boundary, and a designated drop zone or moving to the fairway is not permitted unless specifically provided in a local rule.
